story.head: Strength vs. strength
paras: The Senators won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-1 in New Jersey on Oct 12. The Sens (17-7-3) beat Tampa Bay 6-2 on Friday, and the Devils have won three straight. Going in, the Devils are second in the Metropolitan (fifth in the NHL) and the Senators first in the Atlantic (fourth).
The Devils’ record (.692) is about what their chances are worth. The Senators’ record (.685) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.615), largely because they’re 8-3 in one-goal games.

The Devils draw more penalties than they take (3rd) and keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest). The Senators, by contrast, get into a lot of chippy games (3rd). New Jersey has scored 3.73 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. As for the Senators, they rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (3rd). Something has to give when the Devils’ shooting runs into the Senators’ defense. Beyond that, the Senators hit a lot, but the Devils mostly don’t.

Jack Hughes (11 G / 23 A / 34 P in 26 GP) leads the Devils in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. For the Senators, Tim Stützle (15 G / 18 A / 33 P in 27 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games.
Connor Hellebuyck (9-1-0 / .900 SV% in 11 GS) is in line to start for New Jersey. Linus Ullmark (13-2-0 / .933 SV% in 15 GS) has been terrific for Ottawa and will likely start.
